title: Railway Cloud Services Disrupted After Attacker Spoofs Its IP Addresses
summary:
The cloud host is struggling with intermittent connectivity failures across its infrastructure as external security services block access to its hosted applications. The disruptions are the result of a spoofing campaign in which unknown actors imitated Railway's network traffic to deceive security filters into blacklisting the company's IP addresses.

The outage is the third major security event for Railway in a month, following a breach and an attempted hack of competitor Primcloud by AI agents managed by a Railway engineer. Those agents issued 24 scripted commands and port-scanned 65,536 of Primcloud's internal addresses before the attempts were blocked. Railway has since banned the use of automated testing tools on external platforms amid calls for the company's CEO to resign.

Railway has been having a rough time lately. In one month:
-they’ve been breached
-they tried to breach their competition with AI agents

selectedTweets.bestBit: They port-scanned our whole internal network, all 65,536 addresses, twice.
selectedTweets.text:
- They pulled credentials from inside their app's container and used them to request every secret on the platform: ours and every other customer's.
- They tried our cloud provider's metadata endpoint, the standard way to steal credentials for the host a container runs on.
- They asked the cluster what those stolen credentials were allowed to do.
- They went looking for our databases and caches by guessing their internal names.
- They port-scanned our whole internal network, all 65,536 addresses, twice.
- It was about 24 commands over 15 minutes, done on purpose and scripted. No app was ever run.
- Every attempt was blocked. Nothing was accessed.

AND STILL NO ONE SEEMS TO TAKE IT SERIOUSLY.
